faqs.a: Density is the probability that any cell uses the first color. At 50%, roughly half the cells use each color; at 80%, the first color dominates.
faqs.q: What does the density slider do?

faqs.a: Yes — the X, Y, and XY symmetry modes mirror the random half-grid, which creates balanced kaleidoscope and mandala-style patterns.

howTo: Set the grid columns and rows, and the pixel size of each cell.
Choose your two colors, or press the dice button for a random palette.
Set the density to control how much of the first color appears.
Pick a symmetry mode — or none — for the pattern style you want.
Press Regenerate until you love the pattern, then Download the PNG.
keyFacts: Each cell is filled independently: color A with probability = density, otherwise color B.
The grid ranges from 4 × 4 up to 128 × 128 cells.
Cell size ranges from 2 to 32 px, which sets the final canvas dimensions.
Symmetry modes mirror one generated half across the X axis, Y axis, or both.
Pressing Regenerate re-seeds the generator for a brand-new pattern.

labels.pickOne: Adjust the settings and press Regenerate to create art.

limitations: The art is purely random — you cannot draw or edit individual cells.
Only two colors per artwork; gradients are not supported.
Very large grids (128 × 128 at 32 px cells = 4096 px) may be slow on old phones.
Patterns are not guaranteed unique, though collisions are extremely unlikely.

pixel-art-generator.workedExample:
A 16 × 16 grid with 10 px cells and 50% density:
canvas = 16 × 10 = 160 × 160 px
cells = 16 × 16 = 256
Expected color-A cells ≈ 256 × 0.5 = 128
With XY symmetry, only the 8 × 8 = 64-cell quadrant is random; the other three quadrants are mirrors of it.
